title: Repeating the same work
summary: Use a loop over an array to calculate available stock.

scenario.briefing: The storefront lists stock and reserved counts for every product. The current total ignores reservations and will oversell. Write one loop that computes the true available total.

objectives.description: Compute available stock by iterating over all items.
Prevent a reserved count from producing negative availability.
Check understanding through the remaining explanation and transfer evidence.

hints: Start a total at zero and visit each item in the array.
For each item, availability is stock minus reserved.
A product cannot have less than zero available. Clamp the difference at zero.
Loop over items, add Math.max(0, item.stock - item.reserved) to total, and return total.

misconceptions.feedback: Reserved units are already promised to other orders. Subtract them before counting availability.

misconceptions.description: Allowing reserved stock to produce a negative total.
misconceptions.feedback: A reservation mistake should not create negative physical stock. Clamp each product's availability at zero.

misconceptions.description: Letting an over-reserved product subtract from the total.
misconceptions.feedback: The second product is over-reserved, so it contributes zero. Adding the negative difference would wrongly reduce the total.

misconceptions.description: Believing every loop needs a manual index variable.
misconceptions.feedback: for...of and other forms can visit items without an index. The requirement is visiting every contributing item, not the syntax.

sections.title: Loops process collections
sections.body: A for...of loop visits each element of an array. The loop body performs the same operation for every item, while an accumulator carries the result forward. This is the core pattern behind totals, filters, and transformations.

sections.title: Reservations are state
sections.body: Stock minus reserved is the amount actually available. If reserved exceeds stock, the data may be inconsistent, but the available count should not become negative. Clamping preserves a truthful lower bound while the underlying data issue can be investigated.

vocabulary.definition: A variable that carries a running result through a loop.
Restrict a value to a defined minimum or maximum.

hints: Loop over every item and add its usable stock, never a negative amount.
Availability is stock minus reserved, clamped at zero.
An item with stock 2 and reserved 5 contributes 0, not -3.
Compute max(0, stock - reserved) for each item, add it to total, and return the total.
steps.title: Compute available stock
steps.prompt: Edit stock.js. sumAvailable(items) must loop over the array and return the total available, with each item clamped at zero.

tests.description: A single fully reserved product contributes zero.
tests.name: sumAvailable

hints: Trace both products and submit the final total.
Each line adds max(0, stock - reserved) to the running total.
The first product contributes 3. The second has 2 - 5, which clamps to 0.
After adding 3 and then 0, the total stays at 3.
steps.title: Trace the loop
steps.prompt: Advance through the loop for two products and enter the final total.

snapshots.note: The second product is clamped to 0, so total stays 3.

steps.explanation: The first product contributes 3. The over-reserved product contributes zero because availability cannot be negative.

hints: Select statements that are true for loops over collections.
A correct total visits every contributing item and respects clamping.
Skipping the last array element gives a plausible but wrong total.
Three statements are accurate; reject the claim that a loop must use an index variable.
steps.title: Loop correctness

statements.label: A total must visit every item that should contribute.
A loop must always use an index variable.
An empty array can produce a total of zero.

steps.explanation: for...of and other loop forms can visit items without manual indexing. Empty collections are a normal boundary.
